status_reason: A shortlist can be justified from a published feed-frame example using NIR and Raman fiber probes to predict API potency, so a pilot is defensible. The API identity, concentration range, accuracy target and feed-frame conditions are still open, so the assessment stays provisional.

recommendations.rationale: NIR is one of the two most widely implemented in-line techniques for this kind of task and works with remote fiber probes. A published example inserts NIR probes into a tablet-press feed frame to predict API potency.
recommendations.conditions: Requires a chemometric calibration built on this blend and a workable probe position in the feed frame.

making it ideal for online applications, including remote measurements via fiber optic probes.

recommendations.rationale: Raman gives complementary molecular-backbone information and is used with a contact probe in the same feed-frame example. It is a single-method alternative worth measuring against NIR.
recommendations.conditions: Applies if the blend gives a usable Raman signal without strong fluorescence background.

citations.quote: Raman provides information on the molecular backbone and symmetrical non-polar groups.
Raman spectrometer and Raman fiber probe for contact measurements with 785 nm excitation wavelength

recommendations.rationale: In the feed-frame example, synchronised NIR and Raman spectra were merged and the fused model predicted API potency better than single-method models. That gain is a hypothesis for this blend and must be tested against the best single method.
recommendations.conditions: Only if the best single method does not meet the accuracy agreed with you.

citations.quote: By combining Raman and NIR, these models can predict API potency or coating thickness with higher accuracy and robustness than single-method models.
collected from the same small, even pinpoint, area of the sample.

recommendations.rationale: ATR probes are used in-line elsewhere, so a reader may expect them here, but ATR needs tight contact with liquid or soft solid samples. A dry powder blend cannot provide that contact.

citations.quote: suitability of analyzed samples for ATR measurements, which is true for liquid or soft solid samples and their components, allowing a tight contact with the probe head.

measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: NIR diffuse-reflection fiber probe; a Raman contact probe as the comparison; both look at the powder in the feed frame.
measurement_concept.location: Feed frame of the rotary tablet press, at a point where the blend passes the probe window.
measurement_concept.fiber_link: NIR can use standard silica Vis-NIR fibers; the Raman link needs fibers that avoid polymer-jacket fluorescence. Achievable lengths are not stated in the sources.

citations.quote: Free of Polymer jacket fluorescence for Raman and Fluo- Spectroscopy

spectral_ranges.statement: Nominal NIR range 780-2500 nm; the usable range depends on the instrument, fiber and probe actually selected.

citations.quote: NIR spectra (780-2500 nm) contain predominantly overtones and component bands of fundamental vibrations

spectral_ranges.statement: Raman is reported as a Raman shift in cm-1 with the laser excitation wavelength stated separately; the example uses 785 nm excitation.

citations.quote: The Raman shift is used as the horizontal (spectral) axis in Raman spectroscopy

solution_options.fusion_note: Low-level fusion of synchronised NIR and Raman spectra taken from the same probe location, with one model per method and a fused model. Each block is calibrated and diagnosed separately, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs. A combined probe would keep both methods on the same spot, which alternating probes cannot ensure.

citations.quote: Ultimately, the measurement data must be normalized to a common time step.
One of the challenges of multispectral analysis is the need to simultaneously connect at least two independently operating measuring instruments.

chemometrics_note: NIR and Raman bands overlap, so calibration models are needed. In the feed-frame example, low-level data fusion merges synchronised NIR and Raman spectra into one matrix and Partial Least Squares regression predicts API potency; the model needs your own reference data and should be validated on held-out runs or batches.
realtime_tracking_note: The aim is in-line, time-resolved tracking of API concentration in the feed frame, replacing laboratory checks that arrive after the press. The required time step and averaging must be agreed, because the methods can acquire at very different rates.
future_direction: If the pilot succeeds, a compact optical multisensor or IoT-style spectral sensor dedicated to this blend could be developed for production, as the sources describe for later stages of method development.

proposal.what_would_change_it: If the API sits below NIR sensitivity or the excipients fluoresce strongly, Raman would lead or another technique would be needed; if no probe can be mounted or kept clean at the feed frame, the installation concept changes.
proposal.next_step: Run the laboratory trial on representative blend samples with an independent reference assay, comparing NIR and Raman as single methods before any combined model.

brief_answer: Sources show NIR and Raman fiber probes used in a rotary tablet press feed frame to predict API potency; these are the methods to test first. Start with laboratory trials on representative blend samples and an independent reference assay, comparing each single method. Still open: the API, its concentration range and required accuracy, response time, and whether a probe fits your feed frame.
